name: RBXScriptConnection
simple: An RBXScriptConnection is the link between an event and your function. You get one back every time you call `:Connect` (or `:Once`). Keep it if you want to stop listening later with `:Disconnect()`.
analogy: If connecting to an event is like subscribing to a newsletter, the connection is the 'unsubscribe' link. Keep it handy and click it when you do not want any more messages.
whenToUse: Stopping a function from running when an event fires, for example after a power-up ends.
Cleaning up listeners you no longer need so your game stays fast.
Checking if a link is still active with `.Connected`.
where: Returned by `RBXScriptSignal:Connect`, `:Once` and `:ConnectParallel`. Also returned by `MessagingService:SubscribeAsync`. Works in Scripts and LocalScripts.

terms.event / signal: Something that can happen, like a touch or a click.
terms.connect: Attaching your function to an event.
terms.disconnect: Removing that attachment so your function stops running when the event fires.
terms.memory leak: When a game keeps holding onto things it no longer needs, using more and more memory over time. Old connections you forget to disconnect can cause this.

examples.title: A lava floor that turns off after 10 seconds
examples.place: Script inside a Part in Workspace
examples.code:
local part = script.Parent

-- Save the connection so we can stop it later
local connection = part.Touched:Connect(function(otherPart)
	local humanoid = otherPart.Parent:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
	if humanoid then
		humanoid.Health = 0
	end
end)

task.wait(10)
connection:Disconnect() -- lava is now safe to walk on
print("Still connected?", connection.Connected) --> false
explain: `:Connect` gives back a connection, which we save in a variable.
For 10 seconds, touching the part defeats players.
`connection:Disconnect()` unhooks the function, so touching does nothing now.

gotchas: Destroying an object disconnects its events automatically, but connections to things that live forever (like Players or RunService) stay until you disconnect them.
Disconnecting does not stop a function that is already running; it only stops future runs.

RBXScriptConnection.Connected.simple: True while the link is active. Turns false after `:Disconnect()` (or after a `:Once` connection has fired).
RBXScriptConnection.Connected.example:
-- Script in ServerScriptService
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local conn = Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function() end)
print(conn.Connected) --> true
conn:Disconnect()
print(conn.Connected) --> false

RBXScriptConnection:Disconnect.simple: Stops your function from running when the event fires. Safe to call more than once.
RBXScriptConnection:Disconnect.example:
-- Script in ServerScriptService
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local frames = 0
local conn
conn = RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function()
	frames += 1
	if frames >= 60 then
		print("Counted 60 frames, stopping")
		conn:Disconnect()
	end
end)
